VibePascal v57 Win64 compiler -- a truncated .ppu is now an error, not a hang
Source commit: 1f605f41b3b06a5fa84fb4cb31ee4298fb30907f
Compiler fix:  c31227c8ca  (compiler/entfile.pas)
Parent release: v56 (a187bbac34e1f61154affa5a57e93298028ffc72)
Built: 2026-09-11, cross-compiled Linux x86_64 -> Win64 (-Apecoff -Xi) from the
       self-hosted Linux compiler 6a460e0e02cc3ef71313aa5040c1934e
ppcx64.exe md5:    858DDDD345B11E0122DA4B9D8902FDBB
ppcx64.exe sha256: A9B8F51571B4FBED5C5C61B8D02C1EACC7A46BF73BC4F7D1325A0033FBEE4EEF
ppudump.exe md5:   039506397B32FC5D32EA794821DDB2E6   (rebuilt: it shares the same reader)

WHAT WAS BROKEN
---------------
Hand the compiler a HALF-WRITTEN .ppu and it spun at 99% CPU forever, printed
nothing, and had to be killed.  A .ppu of zero bytes was handled correctly and
said so, which is what makes this a compiler bug rather than "a bad file caught
late".  Partial .ppu files are not exotic: a killed build, a full disk or an
interrupted copy all leave one behind.  On that input the compiler did not fail
your build -- it STALLED it, with no message to search for.

    intact aspelldyn.ppu   55291 bytes  ->  exit 0 in 0.06s
    zero-byte  .ppu            0 bytes  ->  "Can't find unit", exit 1, instant
    truncated  .ppu          120 bytes  ->  99% CPU, no output, never returns

Reported by BuildMaster, who hit it by accident while corrupting a unit on
purpose to build a negative control for something else.

WHY
---
The PPU reader treated running off the end of the file as a silent no-op.  When
it needed bytes and the file had none left, it returned quietly, leaving the
destination buffer holding whatever it held before, and told nobody.  The entry
header is read through that same path, so at end of file the reader still had
the PREVIOUS entry described in its hands and handed that entry back to its
caller -- again, and again.  The compiler's interface-loading loop happily
re-processed the same entry forever.  On the 120-byte file the cut lands exactly
at the end of the source-file-list entry, so what got replayed was the list of
source files: a million identical "PPU Source:" lines in twelve seconds.

WHAT CHANGED
------------
A short read is now an error, and an error is sticky.  Four small changes, all
inside compiler/entfile.pas, the shared reader:

  * reading past the end of the file sets the reader's error flag (the
    exact-fit case, where the last byte needed is the last byte present, is
    still a success);
  * skipping past the end likewise;
  * on error the entry reader zeroes its entry and reports a read error
    instead of replaying a stale one;
  * end-of-entry reports true once the error flag is set, so the seven loops
    in the unit loader that drain an entry stop instead of waiting for data
    that will never arrive.

The compiler already had a fatal for this situation -- "Invalid PPU-File
entry" -- and already stopped on it everywhere.  It simply never got told.
No new message, no message-catalogue change, no PPU format change.  ppudump
already guarded itself with the same error flag; this makes the compiler agree
with its own dump tool.

MEASURED
--------
Twenty truncation offsets of one real 55291-byte .ppu, identical command line,
only the .ppu varying.  NINE of the twenty hang on v56 -- the reported input was
not special.  All nine now fail in 0.05s with a message and exit 1:

    offsets 54 70 77 83 100 119 120 121 200 1000   v56 HANG -> v57 exit 1
    offsets 0 1 20 39 40 41 45 27645               unchanged clean error
    intact 55291                                   exit 0 both, still compiles

Full 1983-test corpus A/B against a baseline rebuilt from this same source with
the same command minus the patch: 1983 SAME, 0 DIFF.  Self-host fixpoint reached,
stage2 == stage3 byte-identical (6a460e0e02cc3ef71313aa5040c1934e).

WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64, with the published v56
exe as the control so the harness can still fail:

    v56 ppcx64.exe, truncated .ppu  ->  killed at 25s, no output
    v57 ppcx64.exe, truncated .ppu  ->  "Fatal: Invalid PPU-File entry: 0",
                                        exit 1, under one second
    both, intact .ppu               ->  exit 0

wine is NOT Windows: it is an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API
running the real shipped PE bytes, so this is execution evidence for the code we
generate, never a real-Windows sign-off.  Nobody has yet run any VibePascal
release on real Windows hardware.

NOT FIXED, AND NOT HIDDEN
-------------------------
Cutting only the LAST 11 bytes off that 55291-byte file is still accepted with
exit 0.  Nothing an interface load reads lives in those bytes, so the reader
never notices they are gone.  Catching that needs a whole-file length check
against the size recorded in the header, which has to cope with .ppu data read
from a nonzero offset inside a stream -- a different and riskier change, and not
one to bundle with a hang fix.

COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY REFRESH on v56.  No PPU format, RTL or package change, so
THE UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin
tarball alone.
